title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the motivic Galois group of motives over finite fields; the facing pages are unrelated typescript. Grothendieck restates a conjecture from the previous pages in a stronger, 'geometric' form.

(1) Strong form. Let G be the 'pro-algebraic' completion of the motivic Galois groups of \bar F_p. Then G is the diagonalizable (Cartier-dual) group of M^0 ⊗_Z Q, times G_m:
  G ≅ D(M_0 ⊗ Q) × G_m.
Here M^0 is presumably the group of Weil numbers of weight 0 (units u with |σu| = 1 for every complex embedding), modulo roots of unity or tensored with Q. Two identifications are imposed:
- the inclusion G_m → G is the weight cocharacter j;
- the character (x, λ) ↦ λ^2 is ε, the character of the Tate motive. Its Frobenius is p = (p^{1/2})^2.
In modern terms this says the motivic Galois group over \bar F_p is the Weil-number protorus P. Its character group is the group of Weil p-numbers (up to powers). It splits as weight-0 part ⊕ Z once p^{1/2} is chosen, via λ = p^{i/2}u ↦ (u, i).

(2) Weakened conjecture, in terms of Frobenius classes. Let λ ∈ \bar Q* be an algebraic integer of the form λ = p^{i/2}u (i ≥ 0 an integer). Here u is a unit away from p, and some power u^n lies in a field Q'(…). At the primes 𝔭, 𝔭' above p that are swapped by complex conjugation, v_𝔭(u^n) + v_𝔭'(u^n) = 0; this is the p-adic shadow of λ\bar λ = p^i. In other words, λ is a Weil p-number of weight i. Conclusion: there is m > 0 such that λ^m = (p^m)^{i/2}u^m is a Frobenius eigenvalue on the cohomology of a semisimple motive over F_q.

(3) Margin: 'Résultat démontré de la théorie de multiplication complexe : Taniyama–Shimura'. The weak conjecture is thus a known consequence of CM theory. This is the existence half of what became the Honda–Tate theorem: every Weil q-number is a Frobenius eigenvalue of an abelian variety over F_q. One lifts a CM abelian variety and applies the Shimura–Taniyama formula for the reduction of its Frobenius. Higher weights follow by tensor products and Tate twists. The weak form is the statement that every character of P actually occurs.
errors: The splitting G ≅ D(M_0⊗Q) × G_m depends on choosing a square root of p (or passing to Weil numbers up to powers). It is only an isogeny/noncanonical decomposition, which the note glosses over.

The condition on u is transcribed ambiguously (field 'Q'(i)'). As written, v_𝔭+v_𝔭'=0 alone does not force archimedean absolute value 1. The intended hypothesis is presumably the full Weil-number condition.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group of motives over \bar F_p is the protorus dual to the group of Weil numbers (weight-0 part times G_m), with the weight cocharacter and Tate character identified
ideas.modern_name: Weil-number protorus P / motivic Galois group over finite fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (oral/unpublished); worked out by Saavedra Rivano (1972), Langlands–Rapoport (1987), Milne (1994)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as known; Saavedra 'Catégories tannakiennes' and Milne 'Motives over finite fields' treat it

ideas.what: Every Weil p-number (up to a power) is a Frobenius eigenvalue of a semisimple motive over a finite field, deduced from CM theory (Shimura–Taniyama)
ideas.modern_name: Existence part of the Honda–Tate theorem
ideas.where_published: Honda, J. Math. Soc. Japan 1968; Tate, Sém. Bourbaki 352 (1968)

missed.claim: Grothendieck records that the existence half of Honda–Tate (every Weil number occurs as a Frobenius eigenvalue) follows from Shimura–Taniyama CM theory. He frames it as the 'weak' (surjectivity) half of a conjectural Tannakian description of the motivic Galois group of \bar F_p as the Weil-number protorus. If the dating to 1965 holds (the margin note may be later), this predates Honda's and Tate's 1968 publications and the Langlands–Rapoport/Milne formulation.
missed.quote: Résultat démontré de la théorie de multiplication complexe : Taniyama–Shimura
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and attribution: an early explicit formulation of the motivic Galois group over finite fields as G ≅ D(M_0⊗Q)×G_m, with weight cocharacter and Tate character, linked to Honda–Tate via CM. It is usually attributed to later authors.

deep.surprise_reason: An explicit early formulation of the Weil-number protorus as motivic Galois group, with the existence part of Honda–Tate flagged as proved by CM theory. Experts know Grothendieck had such ideas, but this written, dated precursor is not in the published record. Dating of the margin note is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: Line 4-5: likely 'le groupe pro-algébrique complété des groupes de Galois motiviques de \bar F_p'.
'Conjecture affaiblie' is underlined; 'λ ∈ \bar Q*' is correct.

The struck lines are attempts at defining λ; the surviving text reads roughly 'tel qu'il existe un entier i ≥ 0 et une unité u ... avec λ = p^{i/2}u, et qu'il existe un entier n > 0 tel que u^n ∈ Q'(i)*...'; 'Q'(i)' is uncertain (possibly Q(λ) or a field containing p^{1/2}).
Margin reads: 'Résultat démontré de la théorie de la multiplication complexe : Taniyama–Shimura'.
Final lines: 'soit une valeur propre de Frobenius de la cohomologie d'un motif semi-simple sur F_q'.
